text: Why do your ears pop on a plane?
speaker: narrator

text: Behind each eardrum is a tiny pocket of air.
speaker: narrator

text: It connects to your throat through a thin tube.
speaker: narrator

text: On the ground, the pressure on both sides matches.
speaker: narrator

text: But as the plane climbs, the cabin air thins out.
speaker: narrator

text: The air behind your eardrum pushes outward.
speaker: narrator

text: So the tube pops open and lets it escape.
speaker: narrator

text: Landing is the opposite, and it is harder.
speaker: narrator

text: The outside air pushes in, and the tube stays shut.
speaker: narrator

text: So swallow, yawn, or chew to pull it open.
speaker: narrator

text: Your ears just matched the sky.
speaker: narrator

text: Follow for the next tiny why.
speaker: narrator
